macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures edge higher as oil retreats after Iran-related shock
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures rebounded as oil prices steadied, with investors weighing renewed U.S.-Iran tensions against easing energy-market pressure. Reuters said the move followed fresh U.S. strikes on Iran and a jump in crude, while Treasury yields were also steady in early trading.

items.title: Treasury yields steady after prior spike as traders await U.S. data
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields held mostly steady after a sharp move in the previous session, reflecting a market pause while traders look ahead to domestic economic data and watch the Iran flare-up. CNBC said the yield move came after the prior day's spike.

items.title: Micron lifts U.S. investment plan to more than $250 billion through 2035
items.summary: Micron Technology said it will expand U.S. investment to more than $250 billion by 2035, citing strong AI-era memory-chip demand and policy support for domestic chip production. The announcement was reported by Reuters.

items.title: Semiconductor stocks wobble on Iran tensions and Samsung signals
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. semiconductor shares were under pressure after renewed Middle East tensions and disappointing signals from Samsung Electronics shook confidence in the AI trade. The move raised concerns that recent enthusiasm for chip names could remain volatile.

items.title: Oil prices jump after U.S. memorandum with Iran is said to be over
items.summary: Crude oil surged after President Trump said the U.S. memorandum of understanding with Iran was 'over,' adding to geopolitical risk in energy markets. Reuters said chip stocks briefly rallied in Asia before fading as the broader market digested the news.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin steadies near $64K after Federal Reserve holds rates unchanged
items.summary: Bitcoin and major altcoins traded sideways after the Fed kept rates steady, with BTC around $64,176 and ETH near $1,909. Trading activity was muted, though markets saw 96,672 liquidations worth $316.23 million in the past 24 hours.

items.title: Crypto market softens as Bitcoin and Ethereum recover only modestly
items.summary: A market recap showed Bitcoin near $63,799 and Ethereum around $1,900, with both up slightly on the day but still down over the week. The total crypto market capitalization was about $2.18 trillion, and sentiment remained in fear territory.

items.title: Bitcoin reclaims $64K ahead of Fed decision as altcoins post mixed gains
items.summary: Bitcoin rebounded above $64,000 after dipping below $62,800, while Ethereum also moved back above $1,900. Larger-cap altcoins were mixed, with XRP and ADA gaining while NEAR, LTC, and ZEC fell.

items.title: Fed rate decision leaves Bitcoin and altcoins little changed
items.summary: After the Federal Reserve held rates at 3.50% to 3.75%, Bitcoin briefly gained before retreating, trading near $63,900. The move underscored the market’s short-term sensitivity to macro policy and rate expectations.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs post outflows while Ethereum ETFs attract inflows
items.summary: ETF flow data showed net outflows of $49.8 million from spot Bitcoin ETFs and net inflows of $14.5 million into spot Ethereum ETFs. The divergence suggests continued rotation in institutional crypto exposure.

items.title: Bonzo Lend loses $9 million in Hedera oracle exploit
items.summary: CoinTelegraph reported that Bonzo Lend suffered a $9 million loss in an oracle exploit on Hedera. The incident adds to ongoing concerns about DeFi security and smart-contract or oracle risk.

items.title: Robinhood says AI agent feature will soon assist crypto traders
items.summary: Robinhood said its AI agent feature will soon help crypto traders, signaling further integration of AI tools into retail trading workflows. The announcement highlights continued product expansion in consumer crypto platforms.

items.title: Hyperliquid and Phantom urge clearer U.S. CFTC boundaries for on-chain markets
items.summary: Hyperliquid and Phantom submitted a joint opinion to the U.S. CFTC calling for clearer distinctions between infrastructure developers and regulated financial service providers. The filing reflects ongoing regulatory pressure around DeFi and on-chain market structure.

items.title: Immunefi says crypto hacking losses hit a new high in first half of 2026
items.summary: Immunefi reported that hacking losses in the cryptocurrency industry reached about $972 million in the first half of 2026. The figures reinforce security as a major sector-wide risk.

items.title: MegaETH cross-chain TVL drops sharply in 24 hours
items.summary: ChainCatcher cited data showing MegaETH’s total cross-chain TVL fell to about $31.18 million, a 59.44% drop over 24 hours. The move points to rapid shifts in liquidity across emerging blockchain ecosystems.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Microsoft sheds 23 Double Fine staff after studio goes independent
items.summary: Double Fine has laid off 23 employees following a move to independent status, according to reporting discussed on Game Mess Mornings. The same report says Microsoft also explained why some Xbox discs stopped working and said a fix is coming.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly losing about $150 on each Xbox console
items.summary: A Windows Central report cited in Game Mess Mornings says Microsoft is losing roughly $150 on recently manufactured Xbox Series X and S consoles because of rising memory and storage costs. The discussion also mentioned Xbox and Ubisoft introducing one-way console-to-PC cross-buy.

items.title: Gears of War multiplayer reveal expected ahead of August beta
items.summary: Game Mess Mornings said The Coalition is expected to show classic 4v4 competitive multiplayer and a 12-player PvE horde mode for Gears of War: E-Day before a beta begins on August 6. The segment framed it as one of the day’s notable upcoming game announcements.

items.title: Microsoft and Ubisoft add one-way console-to-PC cross-buy
items.summary: Game Mess Mornings reported that Xbox and Ubisoft have introduced a one-way cross-buy feature from console to PC. The detail was highlighted as part of broader Xbox platform news.

items.title: Capcom moves Onimusha: Way of the Sword up to September 4
items.summary: The Verge reported that Capcom has advanced the release date of Onimusha: Way of the Sword to September 4, earlier than the previously planned September 25 launch. This is one of the clearest release-date changes in the latest gaming news cycle.

items.title: Double Fine and Compulsion Games go independent; Microsoft sells Ninja Theory and Undead Labs
items.summary: The Verge reported that Microsoft is letting Double Fine and Compulsion Games become independent and is also selling Ninja Theory and Undead Labs. The story is part of a broader round of Xbox restructuring news.

items.title: Microsoft lays off 3,200 workers across four Xbox studios
items.summary: PCMag reported that Microsoft split with four Xbox Game Studios and laid off 3,200 employees. The report underscores continued turbulence across Xbox’s game business.

items.title: Nintendo to stop selling original Switch in Europe next year
items.summary: The Verge reported that Nintendo will stop selling the original Switch in Europe next year. The item adds to recent signs that the aging console is nearing the end of its commercial life.

items.title: Sony plans to make all new PlayStation games digital-only from 2028
items.summary: The Verge and PCMag reported that Sony plans to end production of physical PlayStation game discs for new releases starting in January 2028. The decision is a major industry shift away from physical media.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown after 7 years
items.summary: IGN reported that Nintendo will shut down Mario Kart Tour this September after seven years of service and will not offer an offline version. This is one of the notable live-service shutdown announcements in gaming news.
